## Purpose

This notebook provides a line-by-line conceptual reading of `tests/testthat/test-core.R`, emphasizing why each test exists from a methodological quality perspective.

## Setup

```{r}
library(testthat)
library(tibble)
source("R/core.R")
```

## 1) Inspect test file

```{r}
# Printing test definitions helps reviewers map assertions to functional requirements.
cat(readLines("tests/testthat/test-core.R"), sep = "\n")
```

## 2) Recreate representative assertions

```{r}
# Example: schema requirement check.
expect_error(
  validate_input_data(tibble(a = c(1, 2), y = c(2, 3))),
  "Missing required columns"
)

# Example: NA rejection check.
expect_error(
  validate_input_data(tibble(x = c(1, NA), y = c(2, 3))),
  "contains NA values"
)
```

## 3) Validate model artifact expectations

```{r}
# Ensure prediction and metric interfaces remain stable.
df <- tibble(x = c(1, 2, 3, 4), y = c(2, 5, 10, 17))
features <- prepare_features(df)
model <- fit_baseline_model(features)
preds <- generate_predictions(model, features)
metrics <- compute_metrics(preds)

stopifnot("prediction" %in% names(preds))
stopifnot(all(c("rows", "rmse", "mae", "r_squared") %in% names(metrics)))
metrics
```

## 4) Why these tests matter

- They protect input assumptions needed for interpretable model behavior.
- They catch silent contract regressions in returned artifacts.
- They reinforce reproducibility by making failure modes explicit.
